title: arabidopsis-drem-osdr: a cell-type-weighted regulatory prior for DREM over NASA OSDR Arabidopsis pseudo-time-series
description:
A FAIR, reproducible pipeline that assembles cross-study pseudo-time-series from NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) Arabidopsis thaliana studies and fits Dynamic Regulatory Events Miner (DREM 2.0.7) models over them, with a single-cell atlas acting on the model rather than on its annotation.

The method. DREM attributes each bifurcation in a time-series to the transcription factors whose targets are enriched along one branch, using a static TF–gene prior that is normally binary and tissue-blind. iDREM accepts single-cell data but its documentation states it “is not used when predicting the iDREM model”. Here cell-type context is written into the score column DREM already reads: each timepoint is deconvolved by non-negative least squares against a 183-cluster single-nucleus atlas, and every TF–gene edge is re-weighted by whether its regulator is expressed in the cell types actually present. Each arm is then fitted three times under an identical search and pinned seed — flat, binding-only and cell-type-weighted priors — so any difference in attribution is attributable to the prior alone.

The data. Screening all 62 OSDR Arabidopsis studies yields a 10-timepoint γ-irradiation series (10 min to 72 h, 108 timed samples plus 36 untreated anchors, wild type and sog1-1) and a 3-timepoint spaceflight developmental series (115 samples). The irradiation core is stated plainly as a re-assembly of one experiment deposited under three accessions (OSD-498/508/510, Bourbousse et al. 2018), not as cross-study integration; the genuinely cross-study arm, OSD-782, crosses a dose regime and is held out. OSD-219 is excluded as a verbatim duplicate of OSD-218, re-detected from sample-name overlap on every run.

Two findings from building it. After harmonisation all six canonical DNA-damage sentinels exceed 2-fold induction in wild type and collapse in sog1-1 — recovering the source study's central genetic result before any model is fitted, from a pipeline no step of which sees genotype. And the standard Arabidopsis binding atlas, DAP-seq, does not assay SOG1: a DREM model built on it would produce a complete, plausible, entirely SOG1-free attribution with nothing in the output signalling the omission. SOG1 edges are therefore called from the source study's own ChIP-seq (OSD-496 / GSE112529) requiring enrichment over both the matched input and the no-FLAG control.

Contents. Numbered acquisition and analysis code reproducible end to end via scripts/run_all.sh, harmonised metadata, a quality-control report for every stage with gates that fail the run, figures, and a manuscript built to PDF and Word from one LaTeX source. Every manuscript number is generated from results/ rather than typed, and every citation is resolved against Crossref with an asserted first author and year. Provenance, licence and SHA-256 for every file are in MANIFEST.tsv; large re-fetchable inputs are catalogued but not redistributed.

Licensing. Code MIT; data, figures and prose CC-BY-4.0. DREM is GPL-3.0 and is downloaded at run time, not redistributed. NASA OSDR and NCBI GEO data retain their own terms — cite the original investigators.
notes: Large re-fetchable inputs (OSDR count matrices, the 77 MB DAP-seq peak archive, 265 MB of ChIP-seq coverage, the Ensembl annotation, and the DREM jar) are catalogued in MANIFEST.tsv with source URL and SHA-256 but are not included in this archive. Run scripts/run_all.sh to reconstruct them. DREM 2.0.7 is GPL-3.0 and is invoked as an external program, never redistributed here.
